key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the evidence that the State Government failed to communicate the rejection of the appellant's representation in a timely manner, and there was an unexplained delay in considering the representation.
trial_duration: The order of detention was passed on 11 May 2021, the appellant was detained on 12 May 2021, the order was approved by the State Government on 13 May 2021, and the appeal was decided on 24 August 2021.
legal_representation: Sidharth Luthra, Sr. Adv., Ashwani Kumar Dubey, Manish Kumar, Akshat Kumar, Lakshay Mehta, Ms. Ankita Tiwari, Mayank Nagar, Advs. for the Appellant; Saurabh Mishra, AAG, Ms. Ankita Choudhary, Dy. AG, Sunny Choudhary, Advs. for the Respondents
investigation_status: The order of detention was passed on 11 May 2021, approved by the State Government on 13 May 2021, and the Central Government received the representation on 1 June 2021. The Central Government rejected the representation on 24 June 2021, and the rejection was communicated to the detenu on 28 June 2021.
procedural_irregularity: The State Government delayed in considering the appellant’s representation, and the Central and State Governments failed to communicate the rejection of the representation in a timely manner, which violated the procedural rights under Article 22(5) of the Constitution.
appeal_history: The appeal was filed in the High Court of Madhya Pradesh, decided on 24 August 2021, and then appealed to the Supreme Court, which allowed the appeal and set aside the High Court's judgment on 29 October 2021.
prosecution_argument: The State Government's delay in considering the appellant's representation and failure to communicate the rejection of the representation in a timely manner violated the constitutional and statutory rights of the detenu under Article 22(5) and Section 8 of the National Security Act, 1980.
defence_argument: The State Government was not bound to wait on the Advisory Board's report before deciding the representation and must do so as expeditiously as possible. The delay in communication was due to administrative procedures and did not violate the detenu's rights.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the constitutional principle that the communication of the grounds of detention and the opportunity to make a representation must be done as soon as may be, with immediacy, to ensure the detenu's right to a prompt and meaningful consideration of their representation.
precedent_relied_upon: Ankit Ashok Jalan v. Union of India (2020) 16 SCC 127; State of Punjab v. Sukhpal Singh (1990) 1 SCC 35; Madan Lal Anand v. Union of India (1990) 1 SCC 81; Jayanarayan Sukul v. State of West Bengal (1970) 1 SCC 219; Harish Pahwa v. State of Uttar Pradesh (1981) 2 SCC 710; Mohinuddin v. District Magistrate, Beed and Others (1987) 4 SCC 58
other_sentence_order: The order of detention dated 11 May 2021 and the extensions dated 15 July 2021 and 30 September 2021 were quashed and set aside.
